findings.failure_scenario: The agent's visit branch calls readUrl for a URL the Jina Reader cannot fetch; the API replies {"code":422,"status":42201,"data":null,"error":...}. JSON.parse succeeds, then response.data.title (line 41) throws a TypeError inside the 'end' listener — a plain event callback, so no try/catch can reach it and neither resolve nor reject is called. The agent's await Promise.all(...) in the visit branch hangs forever (or the process dies via uncaughtException), instead of failing catchably. The baseline resolved any JSON, and line 45's own response.data?.usage?.tokens || 0 shows the code knows these fields are optional.
findings.summary: The new console.info in readUrl dereferences response.data.title/url and response.data.usage.tokens without guards; when Jina returns an error payload (data: null) or a response lacking usage, the TypeError is thrown inside the res 'end' event handler before resolve()/reject() run, so the promise never settles and the failure is uncatchable through the returned promise.

findings.failure_scenario: Calling search(query, key) when s.jina.ai returns {"code":402,"status":40201,"data":null,"message":...} (quota exhausted / bad key) makes response.data.reduce throw TypeError before resolve() is reached; the returned promise never resolves or rejects, so any await on it hangs and try/catch around search() cannot observe the error. No in-repo caller currently uses this tool (agent.ts uses duck-duck-scrape), so it is latent, but the exported API ships the defect.
findings.summary: Same defect pattern as read.ts: search's new logging dereferences item.usage.tokens (line 40) and response.data.reduce (line 35) without guards, even though line 35 itself uses item.usage?.tokens || 0; an error payload (data: null) or an item without usage throws inside the 'end' handler before resolve(), leaving the promise permanently pending with an uncatchable exception.

findings.failure_scenario: A user runs the standalone dedup script (`ts-node src/tools/dedup.ts`) with only GEMINI_API_KEY in .env — all the Gemini call needs. Before the change the module threw only when GEMINI_API_KEY was missing; now src/config.ts's `if (!JINA_API_KEY) throw new Error("JINA_API_KEY not found")` aborts the process at import time, even though dedup never contacts Jina. Same break for any other importer of these tools that only needs the Gemini key.
findings.summary: Replacing dedup.ts's local GEMINI_API_KEY check with an import of ../config makes the shipped standalone dedup CLI (the file has a require.main === module main()) now throw 'JINA_API_KEY not found' unless the unrelated Jina key is also configured.
